data.narrative:
David Energy, a Series A climate and energy company founded by James McGinniss, Brian Maxwell, and Ahmed Salman, operates within a sector populated by 9 comparable private and public peers, including Helion, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape. The company has raised $64.4M to date.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and yields a $129M implied valuation, derived by applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $64.4M total raised proxy. Peer-median analysis is not executable; while the Climate & Energy sector contains 9 total comparables, insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers exist to support a meaningful triangulation (0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage datapoints identified). A median anchored only to all-sector peers would lack specificity and introduce material distortion.

The stage-progression methodology supports a valuation range of $109M (low), $129M (median), to $148M (high). This single-method result carries elevated uncertainty given the absence of peer-median corroboration. Key dependencies include: (i) the appropriateness of a 2.0x multiplier for David Energy's specific risk profile and market position relative to median Series A advancement; (ii) the representativeness of total raised as a valuation proxy absent disclosed financial metrics; and (iii) the scarcity of narrow peer data limiting cross-validation. A second-stage valuation update incorporating revenue, burn, or comparable transaction multiples would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
